concepts.title: Major Somnath Sharma: First Param Vir Chakra
concepts.section: A Tale of Valour, Let us read
concepts.definition: Major Somnath Sharma of the 4th Battalion, Kumaon Regiment, led 90 men of D Company against about 500 infiltrators at Badgam, refused to withdraw, and died at 24; he became the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra.
concepts.key_idea: Courage beyond numbers: his last message, to fight to the last man and the last round, turned a lost post into saved Srinagar.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr102.txt, A Tale of Valour, Let us read

concepts.title: The Battle of Badgam: Events in Order
concepts.section: A Tale of Valour, Let us read
concepts.definition: The account moves in order: Operation Gulmarg sends tribal invaders into Kashmir, D Company is airlifted to Srinagar on 31 October, patrols find Badgam silent, the enemy attacks on 3 November, air strikes are called, and the company fights to its last rounds.
concepts.key_idea: Reading a battle account means fixing dates and sequence, from 22 October to the six-hour hold after the Major fell.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr102.txt, A Tale of Valour, Let us read

solution_steps.explain: Place each dated event in order from late October to November 1947.

concepts.title: Valour, Duty and Sacrifice: Theme
concepts.section: A Tale of Valour, Let us read (Medal of Honour)
concepts.definition: The chapter presents valour as love of country in action: outnumbered men hold their ground because one leader shows that duty stands above safety, and their sacrifice keeps the tricolour flying over Srinagar.
concepts.key_idea: Sacrifice is not only dying in battle but holding on so that others may live free; the Honour Wall keeps such names alive.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr102.txt, A Tale of Valour, Let us read (Medal of Honour)

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Valour, Infiltrators and Posthumously
concepts.section: A Tale of Valour, Let us learn
concepts.definition: From context, valour means courage, infiltrators are people who secretly invade, posthumously means after death, and tenacity means determination that does not let go.
concepts.key_idea: Military words like ammunition, casualties and reinforcements carry the weight of the battle account.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why did the enemy wait until only D Company remained near Badgam?

solution_template.explain: Several companies patrolled Badgam and were ordered back one by one by afternoon.
The invaders attacked when the small force of 90 was left alone, hoping to overrun it before help could arrive.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What was Major Sharma's reply when asked to pull back?

solution_template.explain: Ammunition was running out and the enemy was only 50 yards away.
He said he would not withdraw an inch but would fight to the last man and the last round.
